data.title: Implement core tap execution: spawn, capture, write, exit
data.body:
## Goal

Implement the core tap execution: spawn the child process, capture stdout/stderr line-by-line on separate threads, write structured messages to the pool, and forward the child's exit code.

## Context

Pattern follows duplex: use `std::thread::spawn` for stdout/stderr reader threads, `Arc<AtomicBool>` for stop signaling, `mpsc::channel` for coordination. Child is spawned with `std::process::Command` with stdout/stderr piped. Use `BufRead::read_line` for line-by-line capture.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Child process spawned with `Command::new(cmd[0]).args(&cmd[1..]).stdout(Stdio::piped()).stderr(Stdio::piped())`.
- Two reader threads: one for stdout, one for stderr.
- Each line becomes a message: `{"kind":"line","stream":"stdout"|"stderr","line":"<text>"}`.
- Lines are trimmed of trailing `\n`/`\r\n` but otherwise preserved as-is.
- Messages appended to pool using `lite3::encode_message` + `pool.append_with_options`.
- Tags from `--tag` applied to every line message (not lifecycle messages — those get `["lifecycle"]`).
- Start lifecycle message emitted before first line: `{"kind":"start","cmd":["cargo","build"]}` with `meta.tags: ["lifecycle"]`.
- Exit lifecycle message emitted after child exits and output is drained: `{"kind":"exit","code":N,"elapsed_ms":N}` with `meta.tags: ["lifecycle"]`.
- tap exits with the child's exit code.
- `--create` / `--create-size` work identically to feed.
- If the child can't be spawned (command not found), emit a plasmite error with hint.

## Validation Gates

- `just ci-fast` passes.
- Manual: `plasmite tap test --create -- echo hello` creates pool, writes start + 1 line + exit messages.
- Manual: `plasmite fetch test 1` shows the start message; `plasmite fetch test 2` shows `{"kind":"line","stream":"stdout","line":"hello"}`; `plasmite fetch test 3` shows exit with code 0.
- Manual: `plasmite tap test -- false` exits with code 1; exit message has `"code":1`.
- Manual: `plasmite tap test -- nonexistent-command` prints error with hint, exits nonzero.

## Goal

Implement core tap execution: spawn child, capture stdout/stderr lines, pass through output by default, append structured messages, and forward exit outcome.

## Context

Pattern mirrors duplex threading: separate reader threads per stream, shared coordination for lifecycle/exit handling, and append via existing pool write path.

Boundary with `TNRUKT`: this task handles child-exit detection and signal-shaped exit reporting when the child dies by signal for any reason. `TNRUKT` adds the explicit tap-level signal forwarding mechanism (tap receives SIGINT/SIGTERM and relays to child).

## Acceptance Criteria

- Child process spawned with:
  - `Command::new(cmd[0]).args(&cmd[1..])`
  - `stdin(Stdio::inherit())`, `stdout(Stdio::piped())`, `stderr(Stdio::piped())`
- Two reader threads: one for stdout, one for stderr.
- Each captured line appends message:
  - `{"kind":"line","stream":"stdout"|"stderr","line":"<text>"}`
- By default, each captured line is passed through to the corresponding descriptor (stdout->stdout, stderr->stderr) in line-buffered real time.
- `--quiet` suppresses passthrough only; capture + pool append remain active.
- Line normalization trims trailing `\n` / `\r\n` only.
- Per-stream order is preserved exactly as read (`stdout` order and `stderr` order each remain stable).
- Unterminated final lines (EOF without trailing newline) are still emitted as one `line` message.
- Tap does not truncate line payloads.
- Append path uses existing local pool APIs (`lite3::encode_message` + append options).
- `--tag` tags are applied to line messages; lifecycle messages always use `meta.tags=["lifecycle"]`.
- Start lifecycle message emitted before first line: `{"kind":"start","cmd":[...]}`.
- Exit lifecycle message emitted after child exit and output drain:
  - normal exit: `{"kind":"exit","code":N,"elapsed_ms":N}`
  - signal exit (Unix): `{"kind":"exit","signal":"SIGINT","elapsed_ms":N}`
- Tap process exits with wrapped command outcome:
  - normal: same exit code
  - signal (Unix): `128 + signal`
- `--create` / `--create-size` match feed semantics.
- Spawn failures (e.g., command not found) emit actionable plasmite error.

## Validation Gates

- `just ci-fast` passes.
- Manual: `plasmite tap test --create -- echo hello` yields start + line + exit messages and prints hello by default.
- Manual: `plasmite tap test --create -q -- echo hello` captures to pool with no passthrough output.
- Manual: `plasmite tap test -- false` exits with code `1`, exit lifecycle has `"code":1`.
- Manual: `plasmite tap test -- nonexistent-command` emits actionable error and nonzero exit.

## Completion Notes

Implemented tap core in `command_dispatch`: local pool open/create path, child spawn, dual stream reader threads, default passthrough with `--quiet` suppression, and append of start/line/exit lifecycle messages.
Added robust spawn/read/passthrough error mapping with actionable hints and preserved per-stream line ordering with newline trimming semantics.
Validated behavior manually in `tmp/uht6fs-tap-check` (start/line/exit shape, code propagation, spawn-not-found hint, quiet capture) and passed `just ci-fast`.

data.summary: Implemented tap spawn/capture/passthrough/lifecycle/exit handling.

- `POST /mcp` accepts one JSON-RPC message.

- Route is outside remote v0 frozen endpoints; no `/v0/*` changes required.

## Goal

4. Paths like `./tmp/cli-ux-tour-20260227T213013Z-69848/serve-init/serve-token.txt` are long. When --output-dir is in CWD, use short relative paths. Consider just the filename when all files are in the same directory (e.g. just `serve-token.txt` with a directory line above).

- Consistent 2-space indentation throughout.

- File listing: show the output directory once, then just filenames.

Secure serving initialized. Clients on your network can
now read and write your pools over HTTPS.

  Output directory: ./serve-init/

  Files created:
    token   serve-token.txt
    cert    serve-cert.pem
    key     serve-key.pem

  Fingerprint (share this with clients to verify the cert):

data.title: Redesign serve init output with server + clients sections
data.body:
## Goal

Redesign the `serve init` output to be a complete "hand this to your collaborator" artifact, including plasmite-native client commands.

## Background

Currently `serve init` prints:
1. Artifact paths (token_file, tls_cert, tls_key)
2. A `plasmite serve ...` command to start the server
3. Two curl examples (append, tail) with `<token>` placeholder

This is fine for the operator, but doesn't help the remote client. The operator still has to manually compose a `feed`/`follow` command, figure out the right host/port for the client to use, and communicate the token out-of-band.

## Acceptance criteria

- `serve init` output has two clearly labeled sections:
  - **"server"**: artifact paths + the serve start command (existing, cleaned up)
  - **"clients"**: ready-to-copy `plasmite feed` and `plasmite follow` commands with `--token-file` and `--tls-ca` flags filled in. Also includes the curl equivalents.
- The client commands use `<token>` placeholder (consistent with current approach — token values are never printed).
- The client section includes the cert fingerprint (from task 3) so the operator can verify identity with the client out-of-band.
- `serve init --json` includes a `client_commands` array in the JSON output.
- The human output is visually distinct and easy to copy-paste (indented, labeled).

## Depends on

- Task: `--token`/`--token-file` on feed/follow (task 1)
- Task: TLS fingerprint display (task 3)

## Validation

- `just ci-fast` passes.
- `plasmite serve init` output includes both server and client sections.
- Client commands are syntactically valid (can be pasted into a shell).

## Goal
- Redesign `serve init` output into an operator handoff artifact with explicit server and client sections.

## Background/Rationale
- Operators can currently bootstrap server artifacts but still have to manually compose remote client commands.
- A structured handoff reduces setup errors and accelerates secure collaboration.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Human output has clearly labeled `server` and `clients` sections.
- `server` section contains artifact paths and a runnable `plasmite serve ...` command.
- `clients` section includes copy-ready `plasmite feed`/`plasmite follow` examples using `--token-file` and `--tls-ca`, plus curl equivalents.
- Client examples never print raw token secrets; placeholders remain explicit.
- Client section includes TLS fingerprint for out-of-band trust verification.
- `serve init --json` includes structured `client_commands` output.
- Add or update tests for human and JSON output shape.

## Consult Me
- Before finalizing human layout and JSON field naming, share a short mock so we can confirm information design and compatibility expectations.

## Validation Gates
- `cargo fmt --all`
- `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`

## Scope
- Maximize Lite3-native field access in runtime hot paths where we currently round-trip through JSON text.
- Expand performance benchmarks so each promoted README metric maps to a measured benchmark path.
- Define and apply a stable policy for which measured numbers are safe to promote in README.

## Why now
- Current hot paths still include avoidable Lite3 -> JSON -> serde_json conversions (notably benchmark follow worker).
- README now reports feed/follow ranges; we need benchmark coverage and methodology that makes those ranges defensible over time.

## In Scope (runtime)
- Bench follow decode path: replace full-doc JSON conversion with Lite3 key access for `data.sent_ns` and `data.done`.
- Shared decode helpers in CLI/API/ABI: remove avoidable JSON round-trips where Lite3 typed/keyed access can preserve current contracts.
- Keep envelope semantics unchanged (`seq,time,meta,data`) and preserve JSON-first external interfaces.

## In Scope (benchmarking)
- Add benchmark lanes for key runtime paths we may promote: local feed-like append end-to-end, local follow processing, and cross-process follow.
- Ensure benchmark outputs include enough metadata (message shape, payload size, durability, mode) to support docs claims.
- Add one script or command recipe that regenerates README performance ranges from fresh benchmark output.

## In Scope (docs policy)
- Define promotion rules: report conservative ranges (not single-point maxima), specify scenario constraints, and include command recipe below table.
- Keep README table runtime-focused (throughput/latency/overhead), not static configuration defaults.

## Non-goals
- No on-disk format changes.
- No breaking API/CLI/remote contract changes.
- No speculative distributed/cluster benchmarks; local + host-adjacent only.

## Risk & mitigations
- Risk: overfitting optimizations to benchmark harness internals.
- Mitigation: benchmark both micro and end-to-end paths; keep at least one cross-process follow lane as guardrail.
- Risk: docs drift from measured data.
- Mitigation: require reproducible command path and artifact-backed range updates in closeout task.

## Decision notes
- README-promoted numbers should come from repeated runs and use conservative observed ranges (median-centered, with outlier-resistant bounds), not one best run.

data.title: Add --tls-ca and --tls-skip-verify to feed and follow
data.body:
## Goal

Add `--tls-ca` and `--tls-skip-verify` flags to `feed` and `follow` for self-signed cert trust.

## Background

When the server uses `--tls-self-signed` or `serve init`-generated certs, clients need a way to trust the certificate. curl uses `-k`; the plasmite CLI needs an equivalent. Without this, `feed`/`follow` against a self-signed HTTPS server will fail with a TLS verification error.

## Acceptance criteria

- `feed` and `follow` accept `--tls-ca <path>` (path to a PEM CA/cert file to trust) and `--tls-skip-verify` (disable cert verification; dev-only).
- `RemoteClient` is configured with a custom TLS root store when `--tls-ca` is set.
- `--tls-skip-verify` uses `rustls`'s danger API to accept any cert (with a stderr warning when used).
- These flags are only meaningful for remote pool targets; using them with local pools is a usage error.
- Help text warns that `--tls-skip-verify` is unsafe for production.

## Consult me

The `RemoteClient` currently uses `ureq` which has its own TLS config. Check whether `ureq` supports custom root stores natively or if we need to configure the underlying `rustls` directly. If it's awkward, flag it — we may want a different approach.

## Validation

- `just ci-fast` passes.
- Manual test: `plasmite serve --tls-self-signed` + `plasmite follow https://127.0.0.1:9700/demo --tls-skip-verify --tail 0` succeeds.
- Manual test: `plasmite follow https://127.0.0.1:9700/demo --tls-ca serve-cert.pem --tail 0` succeeds (using cert from `serve init`).

## Goal
- Add `--tls-ca` and `--tls-skip-verify` to `feed` and `follow` so remote HTTPS workflows support self-signed deployments.

## Background/Rationale
- Secure remote usage currently fails for self-signed certificates because client trust options are missing.
- The server already supports TLS modes; client-side trust controls are required to complete the operator-to-client flow.

## Acceptance Criteria
- `feed` and `follow` accept `--tls-ca <path>` and `--tls-skip-verify` for remote targets.
- `--tls-ca` configures a custom trust source for the HTTP client.
- `--tls-skip-verify` disables certificate verification via explicit unsafe path and emits a prominent stderr warning.
- Using either TLS flag with local pool targets returns a clear usage error.
- Help text marks `--tls-skip-verify` as development-only/unsafe.
- Add or update integration tests covering trust success, usage-error behavior on local targets, and unchanged non-TLS behavior.

## Consult Me
- If `ureq` cannot cleanly support custom roots + skip-verify semantics without brittle internals, pause and propose an alternative transport/config approach.

## Validation Gates
- `cargo fmt --all`
- `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- `cargo test --test cli_integration`
- `just ci-fast`

## Manual Checks
- `plasmite serve --tls-self-signed` then `plasmite follow https://127.0.0.1:9700/demo --tls-skip-verify --tail 0` succeeds.

data.title: Add stdout/stderr passthrough with --quiet suppression
data.body:
## Goal

Add stdout/stderr passthrough (tee behavior) with `--quiet` suppression.

## Context

By default, tap should act like `tee` — the user sees the child's output in their terminal AND it goes to the pool. `--quiet` suppresses terminal output (capture only). Passthrough writes to the real stdout/stderr respectively (stdout lines → stdout, stderr lines → stderr) so that downstream pipes and redirects work correctly.

## Acceptance Criteria

- By default, each captured line is also written to the corresponding file descriptor (stdout → stdout, stderr → stderr).
- Output appears in real-time (line-buffered), not batched.
- `--quiet` / `-q` suppresses all passthrough. The child's output goes only to the pool.
- Passthrough does not interfere with pool writes (no interleaving corruption).
- When stdout is piped (non-TTY), passthrough still works (so `pls tap build -- make | grep error` works).

## Validation Gates

- `just ci-fast` passes.
- Manual: `plasmite tap test --create -- echo hello` prints "hello" to terminal AND writes to pool.
- Manual: `plasmite tap test --create -q -- echo hello` prints nothing to terminal, writes to pool.
- Manual: `plasmite tap test --create -- sh -c 'echo out; echo err >&2'` — "out" appears on stdout, "err" on stderr.

## Goal

(Deprecated) standalone passthrough task.

## Resolution

Passthrough behavior was merged into `32YHQ4` to keep core tap behavior coherent in one implementation task.

- Default passthrough and `--quiet` semantics are now owned by `32YHQ4`.
- This task is canceled to avoid duplicate scope and a silent intermediate implementation state.

  checked:   0 frames, 0 issues

tour-main: healthy

data.title: Add --token and --token-file to feed and follow
data.body:
## Goal

Add `--token` and `--token-file` flags to `feed` and `follow` commands, and wire them through to `RemoteClient::with_token()`.

## Background

`RemoteClient` already supports `.with_token()` (src/api/remote.rs:197), and the server enforces bearer auth. But `feed` and `follow` in main.rs/command_dispatch.rs construct `RemoteClient::new(base_url)` without ever calling `.with_token()`. This means authenticated remote workflows are **impossible** from the CLI today — the most critical gap in the secure serve story.

## Acceptance criteria

- `feed` and `follow` accept `--token <value>` and `--token-file <path>` (same semantics as `serve`).
- `--token-file` reads and trims the file contents; `--token` takes the value inline.
- When either is set and the pool target is remote, `RemoteClient` is constructed with `.with_token()`.
- When neither is set, behavior is unchanged (no auth header sent).
- `--token`/`--token-file` on a local pool target is a usage error with a clear hint.
- Help text for both flags matches the `serve` convention: `--token-file` preferred, `--token` is dev-only.

## Validation

- `just ci-fast` passes.
- Manual test: `plasmite serve --token devtoken` + `plasmite feed http://127.0.0.1:9700/demo --token devtoken '{"x":1}'` succeeds.
- Manual test: without `--token`, same feed returns 401.

## Goal
- Add `--token` and `--token-file` to `feed` and `follow`, wired through `RemoteClient::with_token()`.

## Background/Rationale
- Server-side bearer auth exists, but CLI remote writer/reader commands currently cannot send credentials.
- This is the highest-priority gap preventing secure remote workflows from being usable end-to-end.

## Acceptance Criteria
- `feed` and `follow` accept `--token <value>` and `--token-file <path>` with the same precedence/semantics used elsewhere.
- `--token-file` reads and trims token contents; `--token` accepts inline dev values.
- Remote targets call `RemoteClient::with_token()` when a token is provided.
- Local targets reject token flags with a clear usage error.
- Help text clearly prefers `--token-file` and labels inline `--token` as development-only.
- Add or update integration tests for success with token, expected 401 without token, and local-target usage errors.

## Validation Gates
- `cargo fmt --all`
- `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- `cargo test --test cli_integration`
- `just ci-fast`

- `plasmite serve --token devtoken` + authenticated `plasmite feed` succeeds.

## Goal

Make the secure remote `plasmite serve` workflow ergonomic end-to-end: from the operator bootstrapping TLS+auth, through startup, to the remote writer/reader connecting with `feed`/`follow`. data.title: Add signal forwarding to child process
data.body:
## Goal

Add signal forwarding so that SIGINT/SIGTERM sent to the tap process are forwarded to the child, and the child's exit status (including signal death) is captured correctly.

## Context

When the user hits Ctrl-C while `pls tap build -- cargo build` is running, SIGINT goes to the whole foreground process group. But if tap is used in a script or with job control, signals may only reach tap. Forwarding ensures the child is properly terminated. The exit lifecycle message should distinguish normal exit from signal death.

## Acceptance Criteria

- SIGINT and SIGTERM received by tap are forwarded to the child process (via `kill(pid, sig)` or process group).
- After forwarding, tap waits for the child to exit (doesn't force-kill).
- Exit lifecycle message for signal death: `{"kind":"exit","signal":"SIGINT","elapsed_ms":N}` (no `code` field when killed by signal).
- tap's own exit code for signal death: 128 + signal number (Unix convention).
- On platforms where signal forwarding isn't available (Windows), tap still works — it just doesn't forward signals. Document this limitation.
- Remaining buffered output is drained after child exit, before the exit lifecycle message.

## Validation Gates

- `just ci-fast` passes.
- Manual: `plasmite tap test --create -- sleep 60`, then Ctrl-C. Verify exit message has `"signal":"SIGINT"`.
- Manual: `plasmite tap test --create -- sleep 60`, then `kill <pid>` from another terminal. Verify exit message has `"signal":"SIGTERM"`.

## Goal

Add Unix signal forwarding so tap relays SIGINT/SIGTERM received by tap to the child and preserves signal termination behavior.

## Context

Primary supported platforms for v0 are macOS/Linux. Implementation may compile on other targets, but this task's behavior contract is Unix-focused.

Boundary with `32YHQ4`: `32YHQ4` already handles detecting/reporting child signal exits. This task adds forwarding when tap itself is signaled.

## Acceptance Criteria

- On Unix, SIGINT/SIGTERM received by tap are forwarded to the child (process or process-group strategy documented in code comments).
- After forwarding, tap waits for child exit and drains buffered output before writing exit lifecycle message.
- Signal termination lifecycle message uses:
  - `{"kind":"exit","signal":"SIGINT","elapsed_ms":N}` (no `code` field)
- Tap exits with Unix convention `128 + signal` on signal termination.
- Non-Unix targets compile cleanly with explicit no-forwarding behavior (best-effort compatibility, no Unix behavior guarantees).

## Validation Gates

- `just ci-fast` passes.
- Manual (Unix): `plasmite tap test --create -- sleep 60` + Ctrl-C => exit lifecycle includes `"signal":"SIGINT"`.
- Manual (Unix): `plasmite tap test --create -- sleep 60` + external `kill` => exit lifecycle includes `"signal":"SIGTERM"`.

## Completion Notes

Added Unix-only tap signal relay using `signal-hook` listeners for SIGINT/SIGTERM and `libc::kill` forwarding to the child PID.
Kept non-Unix builds on explicit no-op forwarding path while preserving existing child signal-exit detection/reporting.
Validated manually via Python subprocess signaling (`SIGINT`/`SIGTERM`): tap exited `130`/`143` and wrote signal-shaped exit lifecycle messages.

- **Exit code**: tap forwards the wrapped command's exit code (transparent wrapper).
- **Message envelope**: `{"kind":"line","stream":"stdout"|"stderr","line":"text"}` — filterable with `--where '.data.stream == "stderr"'`.
- **Lifecycle messages**: start/exit messages with `{"kind":"start","cmd":[...]}` and `{"kind":"exit","code":N,"elapsed_ms":N}`, tagged `lifecycle` in meta.tags for easy filtering.
- **Passthrough**: stdout/stderr pass through to the terminal by default (like tee). `--quiet` suppresses.
- **Pool creation**: `--create` auto-creates the pool (like feed). Default behavior if pool doesn't exist is an error with a hint.

## Message contract

```
seq=1  {"data":{"kind":"start","cmd":["cargo","build"]},"meta":{"tags":["lifecycle"]}}
seq=2  {"data":{"kind":"line","stream":"stdout","line":"Compiling plasmite v0.5.1"},"meta":{"tags":[]}}
seq=3  {"data":{"kind":"line","stream":"stderr","line":"warning: unused variable"},"meta":{"tags":[]}}
...
seq=N  {"data":{"kind":"exit","code":0,"elapsed_ms":4523},"meta":{"tags":["lifecycle"]}}
```

## Non-goals

- No PTY allocation (that's a different feature — tap captures pipe output, not terminal emulation).
- No stdin forwarding to the child (tap is observe-only; the child's stdin is /dev/null or inherited depending on context).
- No JSON parsing of child output (lines are captured as-is; if the child emits JSON, it's a string in `.data.line`).
- Not frozen in v0 CLI spec (same status as duplex — can evolve).

## Constraints

- `--` separator is mandatory between tap flags and the wrapped command.
- Child process is spawned with inherited env. stdout/stderr are piped; stdin is inherited (allows interactive programs if needed).
- When the child exits, tap drains any remaining buffered output before writing the exit lifecycle message.
- Signal forwarding: SIGINT/SIGTERM sent to tap are forwarded to the child process group.

## Goal

Add `pls tap <pool> -- <command...>` — wrap any command, capture stdout/stderr as structured messages in a local pool, and preserve the wrapped command's exit semantics.

## Execution order (required)

1. **Canonical docs first**: update docs of record and spec (`docs/record/*`, `spec/v0/SPEC.md`) before code.
2. Implement tap command + execution + signal forwarding + tests.
3. **User-facing docs last**: cookbook + final help text polish after implementation is stable.
4. **Epic closeout gate**: run the full CI/quality command set before marking the epic complete.

## Key decisions (resolved)

- **Pool refs in v0**: `tap` is local-only in this epic (name/path pool refs). URL refs are rejected with a usage hint.
- **Exit code**: tap forwards the wrapped command's exit code (transparent wrapper).
- **Message envelope**: `{"kind":"line","stream":"stdout"|"stderr","line":"text"}`.
- **Lifecycle messages**: start/exit messages tagged `lifecycle` in `meta.tags`.
- **Passthrough**: stdout/stderr pass through by default (tee-like); `--quiet` suppresses passthrough only.
- **Child stdin**: inherited from tap. Tap observes and records; it does not transform or inject stdin.
- **Signal boundary**:
  - Core tap execution detects when the child exits due to a signal and records signal-shaped exit lifecycle data.
  - Signal-forwarding task adds the mechanism for relaying SIGINT/SIGTERM received by tap to the child.

## Message contract

```
seq=1  {"data":{"kind":"start","cmd":["cargo","build"]},"meta":{"tags":["lifecycle"]}}
seq=2  {"data":{"kind":"line","stream":"stdout","line":"Compiling plasmite"},"meta":{"tags":[]}}
seq=3  {"data":{"kind":"line","stream":"stderr","line":"warning: unused variable"},"meta":{"tags":[]}}
...
seq=N  {"data":{"kind":"exit","code":0,"elapsed_ms":4523},"meta":{"tags":["lifecycle"]}}
```

## Non-goals

- No PTY allocation (tap captures pipe output, not terminal emulation).
- No parsing/restructuring of child output beyond line framing.
- No remote `tap` execution in v0.
- Not frozen in v0 CLI spec (same status as duplex/serve/doctor).

## Constraints

- `--` separator is mandatory between tap flags and wrapped command.
- Child process uses inherited env; stdout/stderr piped; stdin inherited.
- Tap drains remaining buffered output before emitting exit lifecycle message.
- On Unix, SIGINT/SIGTERM received by tap are forwarded to the child process.

data.title: Display TLS cert SHA-256 fingerprint in serve init and startup banner
data.body:
## Goal

Compute and display the TLS certificate SHA-256 fingerprint in `serve init` output and the `serve` startup banner.

## Background

When using self-signed certificates, the fingerprint is the canonical way for an operator to verify that a client is connecting to the right server (and vice versa). Currently neither `serve init` nor the startup banner shows the fingerprint. This is the single most important piece of information for out-of-band credential sharing.

## Acceptance criteria

- `serve init` output includes a line like: `  tls_fingerprint: SHA256:ab:cd:ef:...` (colon-separated hex, matching OpenSSL convention).
- `serve` startup banner includes the fingerprint when TLS is enabled (both self-signed and file-based certs).
- `serve check` (both human and JSON output) includes the fingerprint.
- The fingerprint is computed from the DER-encoded certificate using SHA-256.
- No new dependencies required (use `sha2` if already in tree, or the `ring` crate's digest, or `rcgen`'s cert bytes — whichever is simplest).

## Validation

- `just ci-fast` passes.
- `plasmite serve --tls-self-signed check` shows a `tls_fingerprint` field.
- The fingerprint matches `openssl x509 -fingerprint -sha256 -in serve-cert.pem -noout` for `serve init`-generated certs.

## Goal
- Compute and display TLS certificate SHA-256 fingerprints in operator-facing secure-serve surfaces.

## Background/Rationale
- Fingerprints are the primary out-of-band trust signal for self-signed and private-cert deployments.
- `serve init`, startup banners, and health/check output should all expose the same canonical fingerprint value.

## Acceptance Criteria
- `serve init` human output includes `tls_fingerprint: SHA256:<colon-separated-hex>`.
- `serve` startup banner includes fingerprint whenever TLS is enabled.
- `serve check` includes the same fingerprint in human and JSON output.
- Fingerprint is computed from DER certificate bytes using SHA-256.
- No unnecessary new dependency is introduced if existing crypto/hash utilities suffice.
- Add tests that verify fingerprint presence and stable formatting.

## Validation Gates
- `cargo fmt --all`
- `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- `cargo test --all-targets`
- `just ci-fast`

## Manual Checks
- Fingerprint matches `openssl x509 -fingerprint -sha256 -in serve-cert.pem -noout` for `serve init`-generated certs.
